pr_title: Avoid Exception on Glances missing key
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The aim of this PR is to handle gracefully the case where a Glances sensor is removed server side.
In that case, HA should stop updating this sensor and mark it as Unavailable.
Today, the code breaks (exception in logs).

In more detail, there are three cases where Glances data can become unavailable after the inital setup completes correctly:

1. Request to the server fails, no data available at all => already handled by existing code
2. Configuration changes server side to remove a whole module (eg: fs, network) => currently provokes a missing key error, now handled by this PR to mark sensors as Unavailable
3. Configuration changes server side to remove an item in a module (eg: hide a filesystem in fs module, or hide a network adapter in network module) => currently provokes a missing key error, now handled by this PR to mark sensors as Unavailable

The PR adds systematic checks that the keys used are present in the data provided by `python-glances-api`. If not, the value is set to `None`.
It also updates the logic of `available()` to check for `None` values.

issue_context.title: Glances regularly reports KeyError: 'disk_use'
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have the glances integration installed for monitoring several computers in my household. I've noticed that the logs show many instances of `KeyError: 'disk_use'`. I'm not sure what's causing this nor what the ramifications are but it seems problematic. The logs don't seems to indicate which Glances system is causing the problem but there are over 2,000 of them reported so far in my logs so it could be coming from all of them, I suppose.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

I'm running the latest version of Home Assistant (2024.4.4) and I'm still seeing this error quite regularly. I think it's related to my other ticket (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/110551) about the service losing connection with the host. I learned a bit more today when it went away...

Here's another snippet from my HA logs, this happened right around 4:54pm this afternoon (4/26):
```
2024-04-26 16:54:52.402 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved
Traceback (most recent call last):

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1055, in __async_calculate_state
available = self.available # only call self.available once per update cycle
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/glances/sensor.py", line 286, in available
or isinstance(value := self.native_value, (int, float))
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/glances/sensor.py", line 301, in native_value
return cast(StateType, value[self.entity_description.key])
~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'disk_use'
```
I looked at the remote system running the Glances service. I reviewed the syslog and found that there were entries like this:
```
$ grep "detected capacity change" /var/log/syslog
Apr 22 04:30:09 plexbox kernel: [2717908.623993] loop9: detected capacity change from 0 to 330944
Apr 26 16:54:42 plexbox kernel: [3108197.719219] loop2: detected capacity change from 0 to 113992
$
```
Both these entries line up with events where glances went away on Home Assistant.
First one:
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/1015891/9e7fa0d2-9e3d-45d2-9252-a08d84da1b2f)

Second one:
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/1015891/e4d4e72a-74cd-4dc2-9815-061f154e3feb)

Anyway from some quick google results, it seems that the `detected capacity change` is from a disk changing size, could be swap getting created by a process or something. That seems to cause the local Glances service to update its disk list and I think that breaks the HA integration because now there are new disks that were not there, originally when the HA service connection was originally established. 

I'm running a bunch of docker services on the server that is running Glances, so I'm not surprised that some of them occasionally pop up new swap or virtual disks get changed out.

review_comments:
```suggestion
        data = self.coordinator.data.get(self.entity_description.type)
        if not data:
            self._attr_available = False
            return
```
Then the rest of changes below can be changed back.
Also not sure why it's needed with all this extensive checking for available in the new method you made.

It's not really equivalent as this would only test the absence for a whole module (like fs).
But in glances, some items inside a module can also be removed server side. For example, glances can be configured not to report one of several file systems (like /boot). This would still provoke a missing key exception.
So I think the `else` clause at the end is the safest.

Those checks are needed because they happen during data update, before any availability check. In this PR, we handle the case where Glances answered with some data (no error) but not all data (some modules or keys were removed server side).

For the available method:
I only added a single check on None value to the existing code which was previously in the available() method.
I didn't want to change that logic, but from what I understand Glances can provide a string in a numeric sensor (for example "unknown"). In that case those checks would flag the sensor as unavailable.
This could have just been left as it was as with below we know if there is `self.data` there is also `self.data["computed"]["uptime"]` (even if it might be `None`)

If we initialize uptime here to the previous value, it never gets set to None if uptime is not available in the new data structure.
So uptime keeps the stale value indefinitely which made the new unit test fail.
It's not a big problem as uptime cannot be disabled in Glances (contrary to other modules like fs or network which triggered the need for this PR), so I can revert if needed.

I will come back on this one shortly @wittypluck 
Have been occupied elsewhere unfortunately. Have not missed it
